@alexander.hansen@9elements.com Are you using all the APIs in this file?

yes, they are all called somewhere, i checked out the last patch and grep for them.

> parsePLDMFWUPPackageComplete

is the main use-case but

> extractMatchingComponentImage

is also needed to extract the component from that later on.

> readPLDMPackage

is used to read a pldm package from file 

and 

> mmap_pldm_package

is used to mmap the pldm package from the file descriptor received in the dbus call.

I see following APIs are just generic handlers and nothing to do with PLDM, so please drop word PLDM from there and call it something generic as in future the PLDM image parsing logic will come from libpldm -

readPLDMPackage - readImagePackage
mmap_pldm_package - mmapImagePackage


So, you would be left with just 2 -
parsePLDMFWUPPackageComplete 
extractMatchingComponentImage

where extractMatchingComponentImage will again be high level API to iterate the retrieved data by parsePLDM API.
makes sense 👍. renamed the functions.

I think we need some meson option to safeguard this compilation since you added a conditional inclusion of libpldm_dep.

Let's say the meson option is software-common-code and enabled by default.

We can define a build flag, lets say

build_common_code = (get_option('software-common-code').allowed() or get_option('Updater-X').allowed() or ...)


if (build_common_code)
// Build the common code
endif

The common code will not build from openbmc/openbmc when no package-config (for updater using common code) is enabled.

Also, the conditional inclusion of libpldm will also need a "or" of this build flag.
 
This is a suggestion so you would need to try and we can refine on the nomenclature.
